module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 160

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/160](https://www.erdosproblems.com/160)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos160

/--
Let $h(n)$ be the smallest $k$ such that $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ can be coloured with $k$ colours
so that every four-term arithmetic progression must contain at least three distinct colours.
-/
noncomputable def erdos_160.h (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
    sInf {k | ∃ (colouring : Finset.Icc 1 n → Fin k), ∀ (progression : Set ℕ),
    (progression ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n ∧ progression.IsAPOfLength 4) →
    3 ≤ (colouring '' {k | (k : ℕ) ∈ progression}).ncard}


open Filter

/--
On [Mathoverflow](https://mathoverflow.net/a/410815) user
[leechlattice](https://mathoverflow.net/users/125498/leechlattice) shows that
$h(n) \ll n^{\frac 2 3}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 51]
theorem erdos_160.known_upper :
    (fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n => (n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3) := by
  sorry

open Real

/--
Estimate $h(n)$ by finding a better upper bound.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 51]
theorem erdos_160.better_upper :
    let upper_bound : ℕ → ℝ := answer(sorry)
    (fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] upper_bound ∧
    upper_bound =o[atTop] fun n => (n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3) := by
  sorry

/--
Estimate $h(n)$ by finding a better lower bound.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 51]
theorem erdos_160.better_lower:
    let lower_bound : ℕ → ℝ := answer(sorry)
    (lower_bound =O[atTop] fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ)) ∧
    ∀ c > 0,
    (fun (n : ℕ) => exp (c * log n ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 12))) =O[atTop] (fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ)) →
    ∀ c > 0, (fun (n : ℕ) => exp (c * log n ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 12))) =o[atTop] lower_bound := by
  sorry

/--
The observation of Zachary Hunter in [that question](https://mathoverflow.net/q/410808)
coupled with the bounds of Kelley-Meka [KeMe23](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.05537) imply that
$$h(N) \gg \exp(c(\log N)^{\frac 1 {12}})$$
for some $c > 0$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 51]
theorem erdos_160.variants.known_lower :
    ∃ c > 0, (fun (n : ℕ) => exp (c * log (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 12)))
    =O[atTop] fun n => (erdos_160.h n : ℝ):= by
  sorry

end Erdos160

status_issues.recorded: `@[category research open]`, with an unknown upper bound required to be little-o of N^(2/3).
status_issues.source_status: This particular improvement request is solved. Hunter's 18 October 2025 comment, incorporated into the source's remarks, gives h(N) ≪ N^(log(3)/log(22)+o(1)). Since log(3)/log(22) < 1/2, the explicit choice upper_bound(N) = N^(1/2) satisfies h = O(upper_bound) and upper_bound = o(N^(2/3)).
status_issues.evidence: The Erdős 160 page says, “In the comments of this site Hunter improves this to h(N) ≪ N^{log 3/log 22+o(1)}.” See https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/160#post-1200 and the 9 July 2026 archived page https://web.archive.org/web/20260709213324id_/https://www.erdosproblems.com/160.
status_issues.suggested_change: Mark this declaration `research solved` and fill the slot, for example with `answer(fun n => (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 2))`. Cite Hunter's comment and its Deng–Tidor–Zhao reference. This does not mean that the broader estimation problem is solved.

status_issues.recorded: `@[category research open]`, with an unknown lower bound required to improve the exp(c (log N)^(1/12)) family.
status_issues.source_status: This particular improvement request is solved by Hunter's observation combined with Bloom–Sisask's 2023 improvement: h(N) ≫ exp(c₀ (log N)^(1/9)) for some c₀ > 0. Taking L(N) = exp((log N)^(1/10)) gives L = O(h), and exp(c (log N)^(1/12)) = o(L) for every fixed c > 0. Thus it satisfies even the declaration's full universally quantified conclusion.
status_issues.evidence: The updated Erdős 160 remarks explicitly give h(N) ≫ exp(c (log N)^(1/9)), citing Bloom–Sisask [BlSi23]. Theorem 1 of https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.02353 proves the corresponding bound for three-term-progression-free subsets. Source page: https://web.archive.org/web/20260709213324id_/https://www.erdosproblems.com/160.
status_issues.suggested_change: Mark this declaration `research solved` and fill the slot, for example with `answer(fun n => Real.exp (Real.log (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 10)))`. Cite the improved lower bound. The historical `variants.known_lower` with exponent 1/12 remains correct.

review.notes: Checked all five declarations and found no mathematical defects. In /workspace/review/boundaries.lean, I proved that admissible colourings exist for every n, so the empty-sInf default is unreachable; proved h(0)=0, h(1)=h(2)=h(3)=1, and h(4)=3; and checked the logical simplification of better_lower's conditional quantifiers using the existence of a known lower bound. Finite enumeration also checked the colouring problem through n=9. In /workspace/review/asymptotics.lean, I proved that the proposed answer functions satisfy the exact asymptotic requirements assuming the improved source bounds. Both files compiled successfully. The older known_upper and known_lower statements are faithful historical results, not defects. Live Erdős pages returned Cloudflare challenges, so I used archived pages and read the relevant primary literature. The overall Erdős problem remains open; only the two old-benchmark improvement requests have outdated status. The reviewed file was not modified.
